items.title: Which breakpoint tier is active at a given width?
items.description: Drag the viewport width slider to see which of the listing page's breakpoints (1 column below 640px, 2 columns from 640px, 4 columns + sidebar from 1024px) is currently active — the same three tiers from L1's phone/tablet/laptop/4K comparison. The chart shows the active column count across the full width range, with the jumps landing exactly at the breakpoints, not gradually.
items.compute: var w = params.viewportWidth; var columns = w >= 1024 ? 4 : (w >= 640 ? 2 : 1); return { columns: columns };

items.title: How does clamp() font size respond to viewport width?
items.description: This runs L3's exact worked formula for the listing page's h1 — clamp(1.75rem, 1.125rem + 2.5vw, 3rem) — reproducing the recipe: floor 28px at 400px viewport, ceiling 48px at 1200px viewport, growing linearly in between. Drag the slider below 400px or above 1200px and watch it hold flat at the floor or ceiling; drag it between them and watch it track the line exactly.
items.compute: var vw = params.viewportWidth / 100; var preferredPx = 18 + 2.5 * vw; var clamped = Math.max(28, Math.min(48, preferredPx)); return { fontSize: Math.round(clamped * 10) / 10 };

items.title: Container width vs. viewport width — same viewport, different card layout
items.description: The product card's own container can be narrower than the viewport once a sidebar takes its share of the space — this is exactly the gap a @media query can't see (L3). Drag the sidebar width slider (0 means no sidebar) at a fixed 1440px viewport and watch the card's actual container width fall below the 360px container-query threshold from L3's example — flipping the card to a vertical layout even though the viewport itself never changed.
items.compute: var viewport = 1440; var gutters = 64; var available = viewport - params.sidebarWidth - gutters; var perCard = available / 3; return { cardWidth: Math.max(0, Math.round(perCard)) };
